articles.title: França acusa grupo ligado ao Irã por ataque a geladeiras | G1
articles.standfirst: Investigação encontrou uso de farsi, endereços IP ligados ao Irã e métodos atribuídos ao grupo Shahid Kaveh; procuradores emitiram mandados de prisão internacionais.
articles.summary: Investigação encontrou uso de farsi, endereços IP ligados ao Irã e métodos atribuídos ao grupo Shahid Kaveh; procuradores emitiram mandados de prisão internacionais.
articles.body:
As autoridades francesas atribuíram formalmente ao Irã a campanha de ataques cibernéticos que invadiu sistemas de refrigeração de supermercados na Europa e elevou a temperatura de freezers para até 50°C, em um desdobramento que amplia a crise diplomática entre os dois países.

Nesta segunda-feira (9), a Procuradoria de Paris informou que a investigação identificou elementos que apontam para o envolvimento do grupo Shahid Kaveh e para a atuação em benefício de uma potência estrangeira, que os investigadores identificam como o Irã.

Segundo os procuradores, a apuração encontrou o uso do idioma farsi e endereços IP associados a dispositivos localizados no Irã. A investigação também apontou o que as autoridades classificaram como uma metodologia característica do grupo Shahid Kaveh.

A Procuradoria de Paris abriu uma investigação contra o grupo por suspeita de invasão dos sistemas de geladeiras de supermercados e emitiu mandados de prisão internacionais contra o líder da organização e seus dois vice-líderes.

O anúncio foi acompanhado de um endurecimento do discurso francês contra Teerã.

Segundo a agência Reuters, o ministro das Relações Exteriores da França, Jean-Noël Barrot, convocou o embaixador iraniano para prestar esclarecimentos e afirmou que o país poderá defender novas sanções da União Europeia contra o Irã.

Imagem do corredor de congelados fechado em um supermercado próximo a Nantes, após um ataque cibernético que teve como alvo os sistemas de refrigeração de redes de supermercados francesas, causando perdas de alimentos e incêndios em várias lojas, na França, em 12 de outubro de 2026 — Foto: REUTERS/Stephane Mahe

A campanha de invasões veio a público na segunda-feira (11) após atingir redes de supermercados em diferentes países europeus, incluindo França, Alemanha, Bélgica, Holanda e Luxemburgo.

Segundo as investigações, os criminosos conseguiram acessar sistemas responsáveis pelo controle de equipamentos de refrigeração em lojas e centros de distribuição. Em vez de roubar dados ou exigir pagamento de resgate, os invasores alteraram remotamente a temperatura dos aparelhos.

Em alguns casos, os freezers chegaram a registrar temperaturas de até 50°C, comprometendo a conservação de produtos que dependem de refrigeração constante, como carnes, peixes, laticínios, alimentos congelados e medicamentos armazenados por algumas unidades.

De acordo com a Reuters, algumas unidades tiveram temperaturas elevadas a níveis tão extremos que equipamentos chegaram a pegar fogo.

A elevação das temperaturas provocou o descarte de grandes quantidades de mercadorias e obrigou supermercados a interromper temporariamente operações para verificar estoques e equipamentos afetados.

Além dos prejuízos financeiros, o episódio gerou preocupação entre autoridades e especialistas em segurança digital por mostrar que hackers podem atingir sistemas físicos do dia a dia, e não apenas computadores e bancos de dados.

O caso chamou atenção justamente porque teve potencial para afetar a cadeia de abastecimento de alimentos.

articles.title: GM pagará R$ 1,2 bilhão após acusação de vender dados de motoristas | G1
articles.standfirst: Acordo firmado nos Estados Unidos encerra investigação sobre o compartilhamento de dados de milhões de motoristas com seguradoras. GM também terá de reforçar as regras de privacidade e consentimento dos usuários.
articles.summary: Acordo firmado nos Estados Unidos encerra investigação sobre o compartilhamento de dados de milhões de motoristas com seguradoras. GM também terá de reforçar as regras de privacidade e consentimento dos usuários.
articles.body:
Chevrolet Traverse é um SUV vendido pela General Motors nos Estados Unidos. — Foto: Divulgação / GM

A General Motors (GM) concordou em pagar US$ 220 milhões (cerca de R$ 1,2 bilhão) para encerrar uma investigação nos Estados Unidos sobre o compartilhamento de dados de motoristas com seguradoras.

As informações incluíam dados de localização dos veículos e hábitos ao volante, como frenagens bruscas e excesso de velocidade.

Segundo as autoridades americanas, os registros foram repassados a empresas intermediárias, que os venderam a seguradoras.

➡️ Os dados teriam sido usados para calcular o preço das apólices e, em alguns casos, aumentar o valor cobrado dos clientes.

🔎 O dinheiro será pago aos motoristas? Não. Os US$ 220 milhões (R$ 1,2 bilhão) fazem parte de um acordo com os governos estaduais dos Estados Unidos para encerrar a investigação. O valor será destinado aos estados envolvidos, e não diretamente aos consumidores afetados. Portanto, o acordo não prevê indenizações individuais aos motoristas.

O acordo foi anunciado em 29 de outubro e envolve procuradores-gerais de 35 estados americanos e do Distrito de Columbia.

A investigação se concentrou no Smart Driver , programa da GM que oferecia aos motoristas informações sobre seus hábitos de direção e dicas para melhorar a segurança ao volante. Milhões de pessoas participaram do serviço entre 2016 e 2024, quando ele foi encerrado.

Segundo as autoridades, a fabricante não deixou claro para os consumidores que os dados coletados poderiam ser compartilhados com empresas do setor de seguros.

O Smart Driver utilizava informações coletadas pelos veículos conectados da GM para acompanhar o comportamento dos motoristas. Entre os dados estavam localização, horários e duração das viagens, velocidade e frequência de frenagens e acelerações bruscas.

Muitos dos participantes também eram assinantes do OnStar, serviço da GM que oferece recursos de segurança, navegação e diagnóstico dos veículos.

As autoridades afirmam que os motoristas não foram devidamente informados sobre o destino dessas informações. Em alguns casos, consumidores também teriam sido cadastrados nos programas sem consentimento adequado.

Além do pagamento de US$ 220 milhões, a fabricante terá de mudar suas práticas de coleta e compartilhamento de informações.

O acordo exige que a empresa limite os dados de condução que coleta e obtenha autorização expressa dos motoristas antes de recolher ou compartilhar essas informações.

Em posicionamento enviado à reportagem da agência Reuters, um porta-voz da GM afirmou que o acordo reforça medidas já adotadas pela companhia para ampliar a proteção à privacidade dos consumidores.

A empresa também defendeu que os dados coletados por veículos conectados ajudam a oferecer experiências mais seguras e personalizadas aos clientes.

Como os dados podem afetar o preço do seguro?

Seguradoras utilizam uma tecnologia chamada telemática para acompanhar os hábitos de direção dos motoristas. Por meio de dispositivos instalados nos veículos ou aplicativos, é possível registrar informações como velocidade, frenagens, acelerações e distância percorrida.

Esses dados podem ser usados para avaliar o comportamento do condutor e calcular o preço do seguro. A lógica é que motoristas considerados mais cuidadosos possam receber descontos, enquanto aqueles classificados como de maior risco podem pagar mais caro.

Entre as seguradoras que utilizam esse tipo de tecnologia nos Estados Unidos estão Allstate, Progressive e Geico.

No caso da GM, a investigação apontou que informações dos consumidores chegaram a empresas do setor sem a autorização adequada.

GM já enfrentou outras investigações sobre dados

O acordo de US$ 220 milhões não é o primeiro envolvendo o tratamento de informações de motoristas pela fabricante.

Em maio de 2026, a GM concordou em pagar US$ 12,75 milhões (cerca de R$ 695 milhões) para encerrar uma investigação na Califórnia sobre a suposta venda de dados de consumidores a duas empresas intermediárias.

Em janeiro de 2025, a fabricante também firmou um acordo com a Comissão Federal de Comércio dos Estados Unidos (FTC). Na ocasião, comprometeu-se a não compartilhar dados de localização dos veículos e de comportamento dos motoristas com agências de relatórios de consumidores durante cinco anos.

articles.title: O ‘vilão’ da cesta básica que exige malabarismo para estar no prato | G1
articles.standfirst: Chuvas prejudicaram a produção e reduziram a oferta do tomate, gerando aumento de até 75%; consumidores substituem o fruto por opções mais baratas, enquanto comerciantes tentam segurar os preços.
articles.summary: Chuvas prejudicaram a produção e reduziram a oferta do tomate, gerando aumento de até 75%; consumidores substituem o fruto por opções mais baratas, enquanto comerciantes tentam segurar os preços.
articles.body:
Tomate saladete teve aumento de 75% nas Centrais de Abastecimento de Mato Grosso do Sul (Ceasa/MS). — Foto: Divulgação.

“Estrela” das saladas e dos molhos, o tomate tem pesado no bolso dos consumidores neste início de novembro. O quilo do fruto já é encontrado por até R$ 18 nos supermercados de Campo Grande .

A alta também é sentida no comércio atacadista: nas Centrais de Abastecimento de Mato Grosso do Sul (Ceasa/MS), a caixa do tomate saladete, um dos mais procurados no mercado, saltou de R$ 160 para R$ 280, uma alta de 75%.

Diante dos preços, consumidores já buscam alternativas mais baratas ou até deixam o tomate de fora das refeições.

“Estou comprando a batatinha roxa. Essa está barata. Está compensando mais”, comenta o aposentado Florêncio de Souza.

A técnica de enfermagem Suzana Pereira dos Santos também decidiu reduzir o consumo do fruto e substituí-lo por opções mais em conta.

“É um absurdo, né? A gente que é de classe baixa acaba não comprando. Acaba só olhando mesmo o tomate e não comprando, substituindo por um legume ou uma verdura mais em conta. A gente vai ter que se reinventar ou ficar sem salada em casa, no momento”, desabafa.

Entre os fatores que ajudam a explicar a alta estão as chuvas nas principais regiões produtoras, como Goiás, Minas Gerais e Paraná.

O excesso de precipitação prejudicou a qualidade dos frutos e favoreceu o surgimento de doenças nas lavouras, comprometendo a produção e a oferta no mercado, conforme explica o economista Eugênio Pavão.

O especialista lembra que as condições climáticas já haviam provocado uma alta nos preços no início do ano e voltaram a pressionar o mercado neste período.

“Para ter uma ideia, no começo do ano, o tomate aumentou 25% com as chuvas de dezembro e janeiro. Agora, com outra situação, a oferta foi prejudicada principalmente pelas chuvas, que impactaram fortemente a produção de hortaliças em geral. O tomate, justamente na época da colheita, teve queda na produção e na distribuição”, explica.

O aumento também preocupa quem utiliza o tomate como ingrediente indispensável no trabalho.

Em Campo Grande, a empresária Camila Bertagnolli, proprietária de uma loja de massas artesanais, precisa do produto para preparar molhos e recheios. O carro-chefe do estabelecimento são as massas recheadas, e boa parte das receitas leva tomate.

“Naturalmente, quando você pensa em culinária italiana, seja no que eu vendo aqui, que é uma massa, seja no trabalho de quem faz pizza, a primeira coisa que vem à cabeça é um bom molho de tomate. E também tem recheios, temperos, um milhão de coisas que levam tomate. Então, é um item indispensável e sempre presente aqui na nossa cozinha”, conta.

Molhos feitos com tomate na empresa da Camila. — Foto: TV Morena.

Em períodos de maior movimento, Camila chega a comprar 200 quilos de tomate por mês para preparar molhos e massas. O desafio agora é manter a qualidade dos produtos sem precisar repassar o aumento dos custos aos clientes, especialmente com a chegada das festas de fim de ano, quando a procura costuma crescer.

Por enquanto, a estratégia da empresária é absorver a alta e tentar manter os preços do cardápio.

“Para manter a qualidade, a gente assume essa alta, lida com ela aqui dentro e tenta segurar ao máximo, para ver se o mercado estabiliza de novo e esse item volta a ter um preço com o qual a gente estava acostumada, sem precisar repassar isso para o consumidor. Infelizmente, chega um ponto em que esse repasse acontece”, explica.

articles.title: Pete Hegseth: Chefe do Pentágono minimiza risco de impeachment | G1
articles.standfirst: Após derrota histórica nas midterms, membros do Partido Republicano têm culpado a guerra do Irã — e, consequentemente, Hegseth, o secretário de Guerra — pelo resultado nas urnas. Dissidência republicana se junta à nova maioria no Congresso, conquistada pelos democratas, que terá maior poder de escrutínio sobre o governo Trump.
articles.summary: Pete Hegseth minimiza ameaça de impeachment e defende a Guerra do Irã em meio à dissidência republicana sobre o conflito após derrota histórica nas midterms.
articles.body:
O secretário de Defesa dos Estados Unidos, Pete Hegseth, faz uma declaração em vídeo em Arlington, Virgínia, EUA, nesta imagem capturada de um vídeo de divulgação publicado em 5 de novembro de 2026. — Foto: Pete Hegseth via X/Divulgação via Reuters

O secretário de Guerra dos Estados Unidos e chefe do Pentágono, Pete Hegseth, voltou a minimizar nesta segunda-feira (9) as tratativas para abrir um processo de impeachment contra ele e afirmou estar pronto para defender sua gestão à frente do Pentágono.

"Não estamos preocupados com isso", disse Hegseth, ao ser questionado se contava com apoio suficiente dos republicanos para barrar as acusações que poderiam levar ao seu impeachment.

Hegseth anunciou que dará uma entrevista coletiva à imprensa no Pentágono nesta terça (10), para discutir a proposta de impeachment contra ele que tramita no Congresso.

As declarações ocorrem em meio a uma tentativa do deputado republicano Thomas Massie de forçar uma votação, na Câmara dos Estados Unidos, sobre as acusações que fundamentam o pedido de impeachment.

Rumores em relação a um possível pedido de impeachment contra o secretário ganharam força após o Partido Democrata vencer a maioria do Congresso dos EUA nas eleições de meio de mandato, as "midterms".

Com a maioria, os democratas ganham maior poder para frear políticas do governo de Donald Trump , incluindo projetos de lei e nomeações. A oposição também poderá colocar sob escrutínio as atividades do presidente e seus secretários, além da família Trump.

Guerra do Irã vira "bode expiatório" para republicanos

Após a derrota histórica para os democratas, o Partido Republicano vem tentando se recuperar do fracasso nas urnas. Antes mesmo da eleição, Donald Trump já encarava um índice recorde de rejeição para o mandato.

Entre os motivos apontados pela derrocada, está o impacto de medidas do governo Trump sobre o custo de vida dos americanos. O que tem sido discutido nos bastidores da Casa Branca é qual política em si seria a maior responsável.

Logo após o anúncio dos resultados, o vice-presidente, J.D. Vance culpou o conflito no Oriente Médio, o qual sempre foi contra, pela derrota republicana. Ele tem sido seguido por dissidentes do próprio partido, como Massie.

E a crescente dentro do partido tem pressionado diretamente Hegseth, secretário de Guerra e um dos maiores defensores do conflito.

Hegseth argumentou que iniciar a guerra com o Irã foi uma "jogada ousada" de Trump, "e como o presidente deixa tão claro, você não pode deixar que islamitas fanáticos tenham uma bomba nuclear".

“A escolha era entre não agir e torcer para que tudo desaparecesse ou tomar uma atitude ousada, o que o presidente fez com a Operação Martelo da Meia-Noite, e o que nós fizemos com a Operação Fúria Épica”, disse Hegseth, referindo-se aos codinomes do ataque às instalações nucleares iranianas e à guerra em geral.

A defesa pública da guerra por Hegseth surge após os eleitores terem demonstrado, na semana passada, a impopularidade esmagadora do conflito.

De acordo com a Pesquisa Eleitoral da AP, uma pesquisa com mais de 100 mil eleitores nos Estados Unidos, cerca de 6 em cada 10 disseram que os EUA tomaram a “decisão errada” ao entrar em ação militar contra o Irã, embora a pesquisa tenha sugerido que a guerra com o Irã não era a principal preocupação da maioria dos eleitores.

articles.title: Terremoto de magnitude 5,3 atinge o norte do Peru | G1
articles.standfirst: Tremor ocorreu em Lagunas, entre fronteira com o Brasil e a costa do país. Ainda não há relatos de danos ou vítimas. Papa Leão XIV visitará o norte do Peru nesta semana.
articles.summary: Tremor ocorreu em Lagunas, entre fronteira com o Brasil e a costa do país. Ainda não há relatos de danos ou vítimas. Papa Leão XIV visitará o norte do Peru nesta semana.
articles.body:
Ponto azul mostra local onde ocorreu terremoto de magnitude 5,3 no Peru, em 9 de novembro de 2026. — Foto: Reprodução/ USGS

Um terremoto de magnitude 5,3 atingiu nesta segunda-feira (9) o norte do Peru. O tremor teve epicentro na cidade de Lagunas, que fica entre a fronteira com o Brasil e a costa do Pacífico.

Segundo o Serviço Geológico dos Estados Unidos (USGS, na sigla em inglês), o terremoto ocorreu a 80 quilômetros do solo, uma profundidade considerada grande e que pode amenizar os efeitos do tremor em solo.

A região fica próxima de Chiclayo, cidade que o papa Leão XIV visitará nesta semana, como parte da viagem que faz pela América Latina.

Ainda não havia registro de danos ou vítimas até a última atualização desta reportagem.

articles.title: Monumento de Senhora Sant’Ana em Serrinha inicia tombamento | G1
articles.standfirst: Processo busca preservar estrutura inaugurada em 1955 e estabelece regras para obras e intervenções no monumento e na área de entorno.
articles.summary: Processo busca preservar estrutura inaugurada em 1955 e estabelece regras para obras e intervenções no monumento e na área de entorno
articles.body:
Monumento de Senhora Sant’Ana em Serrinha — Foto: Reprodução/ Prefeitura de Serrinha

O processo de tombamento do Monumento de Senhora Sant’Ana e de toda a área ao redor está em andamento em Serrinha , cidade que fica a cerca de 70 km de Feira de Santana . A iniciativa busca preservar um dos principais símbolos históricos, religiosos e culturais do município.

Inaugurado em 26 de setembro de 1955, o monumento é dedicado à padroeira da cidade e completou 71 anos em 2026. Com mais de cinco metros de altura, a estrutura se tornou uma referência para os moradores e integra a memória e a identidade cultural de Serrinha.

Com o avanço do processo, novas obras e intervenções no monumento ou em sua área de entorno deverão passar por análise e autorização prévia da Prefeitura. A avaliação será feita por meio das secretarias municipais de Meio Ambiente, Infraestrutura e Cultura e Juventude.

A medida busca garantir que possíveis alterações respeitem as características históricas, culturais e paisagísticas do espaço.

O tombamento é um instrumento de proteção do patrimônio histórico e cultural que estabelece regras para preservar bens e espaços considerados importantes para a memória de uma comunidade.

Além da conservação da estrutura física, a iniciativa busca proteger a importância histórica e simbólica do monumento, que há mais de sete décadas faz parte da história de Serrinha.

articles.title: Novo presidente do Paraguai pede a renúncia de todos os seus ministros | G1
articles.standfirst: Pedro Alliana, que substituiu Santiago Peña, disse querer uma reformulação total do governo, Alliana substituiu Peña, que foi destituído do cargo e preso por suspeita de envolvimento no escândalo do fechamento do ueno bank.
articles.summary: Pedro Alliana, que substituiu Santiago Peña, disse querer uma reformulação total do governo, Alliana substituiu Peña, que foi destituído do cargo e preso por suspeita de envolvimento no escândalo do fechamento do ueno bank.
articles.body:
O recém-empossado presidente do Paraguai , Pedro Alliana, um político conservador de 52 anos, discursa após tomar posse como presidente do Paraguai, na sequência da destituição de Santiago Peña em um julgamento de impeachment que o considerou culpado de má gestão devido às suas ligações com o colapso da instituição financeira digital Ueno, apesar de Peña ter renunciado um dia antes, em Assunção, Paraguai , 6 de novembro de 2026 — Foto: REUTERS/Cesar Olmedo

O novo presidente do Paraguai, Pedro Alliana, pediu, nesta segunda-feira (9), a todos os seus ministros e altos funcionários que coloquem seus cargos à disposição. Alliana disse que quer fazer uma reorganização do governo após a destituição do ex-presidente Santiago Peña.

➡️ O ex-presidente está no centro da crise bancária que tomou o Paraguai nesta semana por conta do fechamento do ueno bank, que deixou milhões de clientes sem acesso ao seu dinheiro. Alvo de um processo de impeachment, Peña chegou a anunciar renúncia, barrada pelo Congresso para evitar que ele mantivesse benefícios. O impeachment foi aprovado, e ele foi detido logo depois.

Alliana, que era vice de Santiago Peña, assumiu o cargo na sexta-feira (6), após a destituição em um julgamento político e a detenção de Peña.

"Determinei ao ministro-secretário-geral e chefe do Gabinete Civil, Rolando de Barros, que solicite aos ministros, secretários e máximas autoridades do Estado que ocupam cargos de confiança que coloquem seus cargos à disposição", anunciou Alliana em um comunicado.

O novo mandatário informou que "o funcionamento de todas as instituições continuará com absoluta normalidade ".

O novo presidente já havia iniciado uma renovação de seu gabinete. Nesta segunda-feira, ele empossou Ariel Martínez como ministro do Interior, Juan Carlos Baruja em Obras Públicas e Rolando de Barros como chefe de Gabinete.

Também nomeou novos titulares para as áreas de Meio Ambiente e Tecnologia, além do comando da empresa estatal de eletricidade ANDE.

O mandatário indicou, ainda, o economista Jorge Schreiner para presidir o Banco Central (BCP), cuja nomeação requer a aprovação do Senado.

O governo busca acelerar a devolução das economias e adotou medidas de alívio tributário para os afetados.

articles.title: Lei determina que lojas do MA exibam telas dos caixas aos clientes | G1
articles.standfirst: Estabelecimentos devem exibir valores, descontos e troco durante as compras. Norma também prevê multas em caso de descumprimento.
articles.summary: Estabelecimentos devem exibir valores, descontos e troco durante as compras. Norma também prevê multas em caso de descumprimento.
articles.body:
Lei determina que lojas do MA mantenham telas dos caixas visíveis aos consumidores — Foto: MPCE/ Divulgação

A Assembleia Legislativa do Maranhão aprovou a Lei Estadual nº 12.967/2026, que determina que os estabelecimentos comerciais mantenham os monitores dos caixas visíveis aos consumidores. As telas devem permitir que os clientes acompanhem os valores registrados durante as compras.

A lei surgiu a partir de uma sugestão elaborada pelo Centro de Apoio Operacional de Defesa do Consumidor (CAO-Consumidor) do Ministério Público do Maranhão (MPMA).O objetivo é garantir transparência e permitir que os consumidores confiram os dados antes do fechamento das compras.

A lei entrou em vigor em 27 de outubro, 90 dias após sua promulgação, em 29 de julho.

Na avaliação da promotora de Justiça e coordenadora do CAO-Consumidor, Alineide Martins, a medida visa fortalecer os direitos dos consumidores maranhenses, assegurando a conferência, em tempo real, dos itens registrados nos caixas.

A nova legislação determina que as empresas instalem as telas em locais visíveis e de fácil acesso ao público, preferencialmente na altura dos olhos. Os visores devem exibir com clareza o valor unitário dos produtos e serviços, o total da compra, os descontos concedidos e o troco. Também é proibida qualquer obstrução visual por cartazes ou mercadorias.

Em caso de descumprimento, a empresa pode receber uma advertência e terá prazo de 30 dias para se regularizar. Também poderá ser aplicada multa de até 500 vezes o valor da Unidade Fiscal de Referência do Estado do Maranhão (UFR-MA). Em caso de reincidência, a multa poderá ser dobrada.

Os valores arrecadados com as multas serão destinados ao Fundo Estadual de Proteção e Defesa dos Direitos do Consumidor.

articles.summary: Após adotar tom conciliador, presidente dos EUA atribuiu a derrota de seu partido à votação antecipada e questionou: "Alguém realmente acredita que estas 'eleições' foram limpas?".
articles.body:
O presidente dos Estados Unidos , Donald Trump , tentou deslegitimar a vitória dos democratas nas eleições legislativas de meio de mandato , nas quais o partido retomou o controle das duas câmaras do Congresso, nesta segunda-feira (9).

Após reagir aos resultados em tom conciliador na semana passada , Trump fez acusações de fraude sem provas na rede Truth Social.

"Alguém realmente acredita que estas 'eleições' foram limpas? Como é possível que as pesquisas tenham errado tanto?", questionou ele, atribuindo a derrota de seu partido ao grande "volume" de eleitores que votaram antecipadamente. "Tudo se resume às máquinas, que são muito mais importantes do que o eleitor!", acrescentou.

O presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, observa no dia em que a última viga de aço é colocada no salão de baile, na Casa Branca, em Washington, DC, EUA, em 4 de novembro de 2026 — Foto: REUTERS/Evan Vucci

Horas depois da votação de 3 de novembro, o presidente havia afirmado ao jornal "The New York Times" que estava "disposto a aceitar os resultados".

No dia seguinte, também em rede social, ele minimizou a vitória do Partido Democrata , que além da maioria no Congresso, conseguiu tomar dos republicanos governos estaduais como o do Texas. Afirmou:

"Eu não estava na cédula eleitoral e, se estivesse, teríamos vencido POR UMA LAVADA!"

No mesmo dia, ao falar com jornalistas em um evento oficial, Trump também afirmou que "provavelmente se dará bem" com os democratas e admitiu que a guerra contra o Irã contribuiu para a derrota republicana.

articles.title: Actor Chris Hemsworth became a patron of an Australian children's charity; after 40 years, it has supported more than 50,000 children and young people
articles.summary: Australian actor Chris Hemsworth has used his public profile to support the Australian Childhood Foundation, a charity dedicated to helping children
articles.body: Australian actor Chris Hemsworth has used his public profile to support the Australian Childhood Foundation, a charity dedicated to helping children recover from abuse, family violence and neglect. The organisation says it has assisted more than 50,000 children and young people over four decades, working to create safer environments and provide care for those affected by trauma. Hemsworth’s involvement reflects a personal connection to the cause, shaped by his family’s experience in social work and his own understanding of the importance of protecting children. His support has also brought attention to an issue that often remains difficult to discuss openly.Chris Hemsworth and the Australian Childhood Foundation’s workThe Australian Childhood Foundation describes Hemsworth as a committed patron who helps shine a light on child abuse and its lasting consequences. According to the organisation, the actor has spoken about how his parents’ work as social workers gave him an understanding of the damage caused by abuse and neglect.Hemsworth grew up in a supportive household and has said that this experience made him particularly aware of the importance of safe, loving environments for children. His connection with the Foundation is not simply a celebrity endorsement. It is linked to an issue he has encountered through his family and deserves wider attention.The Foundation’s central vision is that every child should be safe from abuse, violence and neglect. Its work focuses on helping children rebuild trust, recover from trauma and develop relationships with adults who can offer care and stability. The organisation also works with professionals and communities to improve the support available to vulnerable children.Why does the charity focus on trauma recoveryThe Foundation explains that abuse can affect children well beyond the immediate harm. Trauma may interfere with learning, relationships, emotional development and a child’s ability to feel safe. Children who have experienced violence or neglect can struggle to trust adults, concentrate at school or manage unfamiliar situations.The organisation highlights the connection between recovery and supportive relationships. Children need more than the end of an abusive situation; they also need consistent care that helps them understand what happened and recognise that they are not responsible for it.The Foundation says 68% of abused children referred to it are at least two years behind academically, while 77% catch up to their age-appropriate academic level following involvement with the organisation. It also reports that 88% of children do not experience further foster-care placement breakdowns after receiving its support.Hemsworth has also brought public attention and fundingHemsworth’s patron role has also involved fundraising and public events. A Foundation media release dated 18 November 2015 reported that the actor joined more than 800 guests at a Sydney screening of his film In the Heart of the Sea. The event raised $275,000 for the organisation and helped launch plans for a specialised Children’s Trauma Recovery Centre in Sydney.The proposed centre was intended to support children affected by abuse, family violence and neglect. The release described the Sydney initiative as part of a wider effort to establish trauma recovery centres across Australia, following fundraising activity in Tasmania.Foundation chief executive Joe Tucci said children recovering from trauma needed dependable relationships, specialist support and a community willing to stand beside them.The media release also acknowledged the support of Audi Australia, Roar management, Warner Bros Pictures and Village Roadshow Pictures, alongside Hemsworth’s contribution.Rosie Batty joins Hemsworth in supporting vulnerable childrenThe Foundation’s public advocacy has also expanded through the involvement of other prominent figures. Its announcement about Rosie Batty joining as a patron explained that she would work alongside Hemsworth to strengthen attention on children.Batty, named Australian of the Year in 2015, established the Luke Batty Foundation in memory of her son and became a prominent advocate for family violence reform. Following the closure of her foundation, she joined the Australian Childhood Foundation as a patron, bringing her experience and advocacy to an organisation with a similar focus.The Foundation also lists other ambassadors, including actor Liam Hemsworth, former rugby league player Clint Newton and actor Nadine Garner.How does the Foundation measure its progressThe Australian Childhood Foundation publishes annual reports detailing its work, achievements and finances. Its annual reports page provides documents dating back to 2013, allowing supporters to follow how the organisation has developed and how its resources are used.The Foundation reports that, alongside its 40-year milestone and more than 50,000 children and young people supported, its work includes specialist therapeutic care for 3,000 children and young people. It also reports that more than 11,000 professionals have received safeguarding training and that 40,000 adults complete its online training each year.The organisation provides direct support to children while also helping adults understand how to recognise harm, respond appropriately and create safer environments.The Foundation reports that 64% of children successfully engage in a social group or sport for the first time following its intervention.The Foundation’s message remains straightforward: children need adults who listen, protect and offer dependable care. Its work with families, professionals and communities seeks to make that support available to those who have experienced trauma, while helping prevent harm before it occurs.You use AI every day. articles.title: Finland is pouring 100 million gallons of water into a 66-foot-deep basin to create world's largest pit heat storage; one charge holds 18,000 megawatt-hours of heat and could supply water to around 20,000 people at a time
articles.summary: Finnish city of Hyvinkaa with about 47,000 residents is filling a former gravel pit with roughly 100 million gallons of tap water.
articles.body: Finnish city of Hyvinkaa with about 47,000 residents is filling a former gravel pit with roughly 100 million gallons of tap water. The 380,000 cubic metres will fill a 66-foot-deep basin to form a giant heat storage that the local utility calls the world's largest pit thermal energy storage, according to a report by Ecoticias.Hyvinkään Lämpövoima Oy, the city’s municipal heating company, expects the reservoir to cover close to a quarter of local heat demand. Water from the city mains began flowing in early October 2026 and the filling is expected to last until late April 2027.Preparing for the wintersThe basin is located in the Kulomaki gravel pit and reaches about 66 feet deep. Its cover will measure 738 by 541 feet (225 by 165 meters). The utility compares that area to about five soccer fields. Inside, the water will stay between 104°F and 194°F (40°C and 90°C). Three diffusers set at different heights move it in and out of the basin. During charging, pumps pull cold water from the bottom and send it through a heat exchanger. It returns warm through the top diffuser, and discharging reverses that path. According to the project page, a middle diffuser is kept for a future heat pump or for cooler waste heat of around 158°F (70°C).Finnish summers bring plenty of cheap electricity but little need for heating. The utility will charge the store with heat from electric boilers and nearby industrial waste heat when energy costs little. In winter, when demand and prices peak, that heat goes into the district heating network.“Once completed, the heat storage facility will above all mean more stable heating prices for residents of Hyvinkää,” CEO Sanna Kytömäki said in the utility’s October announcement. With the boilers, the company adds, the network can drop fossil fuels almost entirely.18,000 megawatt-hours per chargeOne full charge holds about 18,000 megawatt-hours of heat. The utility says that could warm about 1,000 detached houses for a year. It could also supply hot tap water to around 20,000 people over the same period. A second figure, 90,000 to 100,000 megawatt-hours, is the heat expected to pass through the store each year. Operators will charge and drain it again and again. Its maximum charging and discharging power of 60 megawatts sets how fast it can respond on a cold day.Since the site lies in a groundwater area, the project's water permit needs close monitoring. The basin floor and embankments use a double liner with leak wells to flag any failure. Divers or a robot could repair a leak, the utility says. Warmer groundwater next to the basin is the main environmental risk the company lists. A separate aquifer system with heat pumps will collect heat that seeps into the ground below. That cools the groundwater and sends the recovered energy into the network, while 18 new observation pipes track conditions on the site and nearby.The project costs €33 million at current exchange rates. Finland’s Ministry of Economic Affairs and Employment granted roughly €7.7 million in investment aid. The company expects fuel savings of several million euros a year and about 4,850 U.S. tons (4,400 metric tons) less carbon dioxide annually.Those numbers are projections for a basin that has not stored any heat yet. Crews still have to build the permanent cover between April and October 2027. Since charging can start only in late summer 2027, it is yet to be seen how much heat the water will lose over the months. In October, Kytömäki said construction was halfway done and on schedule, with no accidents on the site.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: 'Why spend on R&D?' Rajeev Chandrasekhar mocks China's 'easier way' over Nvidia spy claim
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) leader Rajeev Chandrasekhar quipped as China has came under scrutiny over the alleged honeytrapping of Nvidia
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) leader Rajeev Chandrasekhar quipped as China has came under scrutiny over the alleged honeytrapping of Nvidia chief Jensen Huang, who was reportedly in touch with a Chinese national."Why spend money on R&D when you have an easier, cheaper, faster way to access tech through Honeytrapping ?" the former Rajya Sabha member wrote on X as the developments has redemonstrated the growing national security risks as the US and China compete for dominance in artificial intelligence, with access to sensitive technology emerging as a key battleground.Kerala BJP chief said: "For China the ends justify their means - any means, any way - that’s their way. No global ethics or norms like Trust apply to them. Anyone who has studied Tech history of last 3 decades and Chinas rise will also learn about the “China way”."The leader also highlighted his 6-year-old X post, claiming how "China has harvested (aka stolen) most of its tech from - this Tech proliferation has been helped by people from those countries eithrr [sic] deliberately or stealing." China rejects espionage allegationsChina has rejected allegations that it was involved in an espionage operation targeting Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, calling the claims baseless and a “smearing”."The narrative of a so-called Chinese spy is entirely baseless vilification and smearing.", foreign ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said during a media briefing, as quoted by AFP.The denial comes as Nvidia’s board has launched an independent investigation into reports that Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence operation involving Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based data centre company Megaspeed. US authorities reportedly suspect that she was recruited by China’s Ministry of State Security to gather information about the Nvidia chief and the company.The allegations have also drawn scrutiny to Megaspeed, which buys Nvidia’s AI chips and has been investigated over suspicions that it helped Beijing gain access to advanced processors restricted from export to China.Huang recently admitted in a message to Nvidia employees that he had been unfaithful to his wife and apologised to his family and colleagues, without naming the woman involved. Nvidia’s board said it had no reason to believe that US national security or the company’s secrets had been compromised, but would examine all available information. Huang has backed the investigation and agreed to cooperate.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Canada hits Russia with fresh sanctions targeting missile tech, cyber networks
articles.summary: Canada has announced fresh sanctions against Russia, targeting 38 entities and 24 individuals, including those involved in ballistic missile technology
articles.body: Canada has announced fresh sanctions against Russia, targeting 38 entities and 24 individuals, including those involved in ballistic missile technology development, cyber activities and financial networks supporting Moscow's war economy.The sanctions were announced on Monday by Canada's foreign affairs minister Anita Anand on the sidelines of the G7 Foreign Ministers' Meeting in Paris.The latest measures, imposed under Canada's Special Economic Measures (Russia) Regulations, seek to weaken Russia's defence industrial base and restrict its ability to sustain military operations in Ukraine.The targeted entities and individuals include actors involved in developing ballistic missile technology and Russia's cyber activities. The measures will also target financial enablers, including cryptocurrency exchanges, that help Russia evade sanctions and finance its war effort.Canada said the sanctions were aimed at constraining Russia's ability to carry out strikes against civilian targets in Ukraine while increasing the economic costs of its invasion."Canada is taking action to undermine Putin's capacity to strike Ukrainian cities with its missiles. We remain steadfast in our support for Ukraine and will continue to impose costs on Russia until it ends its aggression and respects Ukraine's sovereignty and territorial integrity," Anand said.The Canadian government said it would continue working with allies and partners to increase pressure on individuals and entities supporting Russia's military operations.It also reiterated its commitment to supporting Ukraine and pursuing a just and lasting peace in line with the principles of the United Nations Charter.You use AI every day. articles.title: A dog found wandering in Connecticut had bullet fragments lodged in her face; rescuers named her Gracie, vets say she is improving, and animal advocates have offered a $6,000 reward for information
articles.summary: In heartbreaking news from Connecticut, a rescued dog named Gracie has been shot in the face.
articles.body: In heartbreaking news from Connecticut, a rescued dog named Gracie has been shot in the face. She is a female pitbull mix, and was found wandering around Waterbury, Connecticut, with bullet fragments lodged in her face. She had been spotted roaming the area for several days before animal rescuers managed to bring her to safety. What they discovered after her rescue was far worse than anyone had anticipated. While Gracie is now receiving medical attention and showing signs of improvement, animal welfare organisations are determined to find the person responsible for hurting her.A rescue that uncovered something horrificGracie was first spotted wandering around Fulton Park in Waterbury, where residents had reported seeing the dog moving around the neighbourhood. She was frightened and difficult to approach, making it challenging for rescuers to bring her in. Several attempts were made to capture her, but she managed to get away.On October 30, Waterbury Animal Control, with assistance from the CT Dog Gone Recovery Volunteer Network, finally managed to rescue her. The tan-and-white pit bull mix was taken in for medical attention, where veterinary technicians made a disturbing discovery. Gracie had bullet fragments embedded in her face.Further examinations and X-rays at VCA Shoreline Veterinary Referral and Emergency Center in Shelton confirmed that she had been shot with a high-velocity pistol. The bullet had disintegrated upon impact, leaving several fragments lodged in her face.She had complicated injuries because of where the fragments had settled. According to Waterbury Woof Pack, a nonprofit that helped coordinate her care, removing them would require taking out significant portions of her sinus tissue. Her veterinarians therefore decided that attempting to remove the fragments could cause more harm than leaving them in place.Her wound also cannot be completely closed at present, meaning that her recovery will require careful monitoring, daily wound care, medication and multiple follow-up veterinary appointments. It is a long road ahead for a dog who has already been through so much.A little kindness goes a long wayDespite the severity of her injuries, Gracie seems to be responding well to treatment. She was eventually transferred to the Animal Rescue Foundation (ARF) in Terryville, where she is receiving round-the-clock attention and care from volunteers.Holly Goodwin, president of the foundation, has shared encouraging updates about her recovery. Gracie is on medication to manage her pain, but that has not stopped her from showing glimpses of the happy dog she might have been all along.When rescuers first got to see her settling into her new surroundings, she was already walking around the yard, jumping about and wagging her tail. Goodwin described her as a particularly sweet dog who was becoming comfortable in her new environment.It is difficult not to feel moved by that image. After spending days wandering around unfamiliar streets with such serious injuries, Gracie is finally somewhere she does not have to fend for herself. There are people watching over her, making sure she gets her medication, tending to her wounds and giving her the time she needs to heal.Goodwin is hopeful that Gracie will make a full recovery, although it may take a couple of months of close supervision. Once she is well enough, the foundation hopes to put her up for adoption so that she can find a permanent home.For now, the priority is making sure she is healthy, comfortable and surrounded by people who treat her with the kindness she deserves.A $6,000 reward to find whoever hurt herWhile Gracie's recovery is encouraging, the circumstances surrounding her injuries remain deeply troubling. Waterbury police have begun investigating the incident, trying to establish who shot her and whether the person responsible also abandoned her.Animal welfare organisation Desmond's Army Animal Law Advocates has announced a $6,000 reward for information leading to the arrest and prosecution of the person responsible. The amount includes $5,000 contributed by Desmond's Army and another $1,000 from Army's Legacy Animal Rescue and Sanctuary.The organisations are appealing to anyone who might know where Gracie previously lived, who may have been responsible for her care or who has information about the shooting to come forward.Anyone with information can contact the Waterbury Police Detective Bureau at 203-574-6941 or leave an anonymous tip through the Crime Stoppers hotline at 203-755-1234.Meanwhile, the local community has also stepped forward to help with Gracie's medical expenses. Waterbury Woof Pack's fundraising efforts have received donations from people hoping to make her recovery a little easier.A second chance at a happier lifeThe most heartbreaking part of the story is knowing that Gracie cannot tell us what happened to her. She cannot explain where she was hurt, who hurt her or how long she spent trying to find somewhere safe. All it can do is hope that the next person it encounters will be kinder than the last.The Waterbury community has made great efforts to ensure her speedy recovery and the perpetrator responsible gets caught as soon as possible. We can hope this story does not have to end with the cruelty she experienced. Somewhere ahead, there could be a warm bed, a family waiting at the door and a lifetime of walks without fear.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Harrison Ford and Calista Flockhart are set to receive their first joint philanthropy award on November 18; the charity honouring them has raised over $70 million for hospital programmes in Los Angeles
articles.summary: Some of Hollywood's most enduring partnerships extend far beyond the screen, finding their purpose in causes that make a difference to people's lives.
articles.body: Some of Hollywood's most enduring partnerships extend far beyond the screen, finding their purpose in causes that make a difference to people's lives. For Harrison Ford and Calista Flockhart, their shared journey has included decades of individual professional achievements and a sustained commitment to philanthropy. Now, the couple is preparing to step into the spotlight together for a special recognition that celebrates both.A first joint honour for the Hollywood coupleAccording to Parade, Ford and Flockhart will receive the Hollywood Icon Award at the Women’s Guild Cedars-Sinai Stardust Ball on November 18. The event will take place at the Beverly Wilshire Hotel in Los Angeles and marks the first time the couple will be honoured together with an award.The recognition celebrates their distinguished careers and longstanding involvement in charitable initiatives. According to The Hollywood Reporter, media entrepreneur Byron Allen will also be recognised at the event, receiving a humanitarian award for his contributions towards expanding representation, creating opportunities and supporting underserved communities.A shared desire to changeFord has donated heavily to environmental and humanitarian causes. The actor joined the board of Conservation International in 1991 and is currently its vice chair, making him the organisation's longest-serving board member.His environmental advocacy has also included public service campaigns encouraging conservation and greater public participation in protecting the natural world. As reported by The Hollywood Reporter, Ford received the inaugural E.O. Wilson Legacy Award for Transformative Conservation Leadership during Half-Earth Day 2025.His contribution extends to humanitarian efforts as well. An accomplished pilot, Ford has participated in search-and-rescue operations and transported medical professionals and supplies to relief efforts in Haiti. He has also supported organisations including Operation Smile, Special Olympics and Wings of Hope, adds the report by Parade.Flockhart has pursued charitable initiatives with a focus on preventing violence against women and children, improving health and supporting animal welfare. Parade reports that she has been associated with organisations such as For Goodness Sakes, Peace Over Violence and the Violence Intervention Program.From a Golden Globes meeting to marriageThe couple first met at the Golden Globes in 2002, where Ford received the Cecil B. DeMille Award for lifetime achievement. Their relationship eventually led to marriage on June 15, 2010, at the Governor's Mansion in Santa Fe, New Mexico.Flockhart had adopted their son, Liam, before meeting Ford. Despite maintaining a relatively private relationship over the years, the two have increasingly appeared together at prominent entertainment events in 2026, including the Lucas Museum of Narrative Art opening and the Actor Awards.A fundraiser supporting children's health and neurological careBeyond celebrating the honourees, the Stardust Ball serves an important fundraising purpose. The Women’s Guild Cedars-Sinai has raised more than $70 million for Cedars-Sinai Medical Center in Los Angeles.According to The Hollywood Reporter, proceeds from the event will benefit the Women’s Guild Neurology Project and the Women’s Guild Distinguished Chair in Pediatrics at Guerin Children’s, part of the hospital's latest expansion.For Ford and Flockhart, the upcoming recognition represents an opportunity to celebrate their individual legacies while bringing attention to the charitable causes they have supported throughout their lives.Images Courtesy: istock and Instagram/gettyimagesYou use AI every day. articles.title: A North Carolina father sought $3,000 or extra custody days before agreeing to let his ex-wife take their two children abroad; an appeals court upheld a procedure allowing disputed travel requests to be reviewed
articles.summary: A father who demanded $3,000 or extra custody days before allowing his former wife to take their children abroad for a holiday was acting out of personal
articles.body: A father who demanded $3,000 or extra custody days before allowing his former wife to take their children abroad for a holiday was acting out of personal frustration rather than putting the children's best interests first, a court has found. The North Carolina Court of Appeals ruled on 4 November 2026 that a parenting coordinator had the legal authority to step in and create an independent review process for international travel requests. The decision ended a long-running disagreement between the divorced parents. In Fey v. Fey (Docket No. COA26-375), the court explained how North Carolina handles repeated disagreements between parents over children's overseas trips. Judge Valerie Zachary wrote the opinion for the three-judge appeals panel, which upheld the trial court's decision approving the coordinator's travel rules. The ruling confirms that parenting coordinators can create clear, step-by-step procedures to resolve disagreements between parents, as long as those procedures follow the existing custody orders.Origins of the parental disputeEdward Fey and Jennifer Fey were formerly married and have two minor children together. Their custody and visitation arrangements were officially set on 4 April 2022, when the Forsyth County District Court issued a consent custody order. The original order required both parents to put their children's physical and emotional well-being first. It also clearly stated that either parent needed the other's agreement before taking the children on an international trip. To help manage disagreements and make sure both parents followed the custody agreement, they jointly appointed a parenting coordinator on 29 April 2022. Under North Carolina law, courts or parents can appoint parenting coordinators to handle ongoing disagreements in difficult custody cases. Problems grew when Jennifer Fey asked for permission to take the children abroad for holidays. Edward Fey repeatedly refused to agree to the trips. According to legal commentary by attorney Guy J. Vitetta of Settlyd, a review of the court filings showed that the father's refusals were not based on safety concerns or a genuine fear that the children might be taken abroad and not returned. Instead, the parenting coordinator reported that Edward Fey wanted money or changes to the custody schedule in exchange for his approval. He demanded either four extra custody days or $3,000 for each trip. With the parents unable to reach an agreement, Jennifer Fey took the international travel dispute to their appointed parenting coordinator and asked for a formal decision.The parenting coordinator's travel protocolOn 22 April 2025, the parenting coordinator issued a formal decision to create a clear process for handling future international travel disagreements without repeatedly going to court.The coordinator introduced a set of rules and deadlines for all future trips abroad:The parent planning to travel must give the other parent written notice in advance, including the proposed travel dates and destination.The parent who is not travelling has five days to respond in writing with approval or specific reasons for objecting.If the other parent refuses permission or does not respond within five days, the dispute must be sent to the parenting coordinator for a binding administrative decision.The rules also set firm deadlines for sharing flight bookings, detailed travel plans, and arrangements for exchanging the children's passports and signed travel consent documents.Edward Fey immediately challenged the decision. He filed a motion with the district court, arguing that the coordinator had wrongly changed the original consent custody order. He also argued that this had been done without a formal legal motion or proof of a major change in circumstances. The Forsyth County District Court rejected his challenge and upheld the coordinator's decision. Edward Fey then appealed to the North Carolina Court of Appeals. He was represented by attorney John C. Vermitsky of Morrow, Vermitsky, Costello Law Group, PLLC.Court of Appeals upholds the review mechanismIn a published opinion issued on 4 November 2026, the North Carolina Court of Appeals rejected Edward Fey's arguments and upheld the lower court's decision. Writing for the court, Judge Valerie Zachary found that the parenting coordinator had acted within the legal powers given to her. The appeals court pointed to Section 50-92 of the North Carolina General Statutes. This law allows parenting coordinators to help parents follow custody orders and settle disagreements that are not specifically covered by the original agreement. "The Parenting Coordinator acted within the scope of her authority, the trial court did not err in affirming the Parenting Coordinator Decision," Judge Zachary wrote in the court's opinion.The judges found that the travel rules did not change the basic custody or visitation rights set out in the April 2022 agreement. Instead, they created a practical process for making sure travel decisions followed the requirement to put the children's best interests first. The court also noted that Edward Fey's demand for $3,000 or extra custody days showed that his objections were based on personal financial and fairness concerns, rather than genuine worries about the children's safety. The parenting coordinator had found no reliable evidence that Jennifer Fey presented any safety risk or risk of taking the children abroad and failing to return.Broader impact on North Carolina custody lawThe appeals court's decision in Fey v. Fey provides further guidance on what parenting coordinators can and cannot do in North Carolina family law cases. Under Sections 50-91 and 50-92 of the state's General Statutes, parenting coordinators cannot change the main custody arrangements, increase or reduce child support payments, or permanently move children to another location without court approval. However, the appeals court made clear that creating procedures to resolve repeated disagreements over international travel is within a coordinator's legal powers. Reporting by legal news service LAWS noted that the ruling sets an important precedent for protecting children's travel opportunities when one parent tries to use the other parent's consent as a way to gain money or personal benefits. By upholding the coordinator's travel process, the court made clear that parents cannot refuse permission for international trips without a valid reason when there are no genuine safety or travel concerns. The decision also shows that North Carolina appeals courts will support binding administrative decisions that put children's emotional and social well-being ahead of ongoing disputes between parents.You use AI every day. articles.title: An Alabama neighborhood went nearly 70 years without a grocery store, so residents turned urban gardens and $30,000 in grassroots contributions into a $1 million community market that opened this weekend
articles.summary: Residents of Fountain Heights in Birmingham, Alabama, have a grocery store in their neighbourhood for the first time in nearly 70 years.
articles.body: Residents of Fountain Heights in Birmingham, Alabama, have a grocery store in their neighbourhood for the first time in nearly 70 years. The We All Eat Market opened on November 7 after years of work by a local farming cooperative and community members.According to WVTM 13, for generations, residents had to travel outside the neighbourhood to buy groceries, including fresh food. The new market aims to make everyday shopping easier by bringing locally sourced produce and other essential items closer to their homes.The project was developed by Fountain Heights Farms Cooperative, which began in 2016 with the aim of building a sustainable local food system. What started with neighbourhood gardens gradually expanded into a network of urban farms. The cooperative later decided to use its farming activities to address the lack of a grocery store in the area.The market is part of the cooperative's new Heart of the Farm facility at 1201 16th Street North. It brings together a grocery store and a community kitchen. Its opening was marked by a public celebration and ribbon-cutting ceremony on November 7.Christopher Gooden, co-founder of Fountain Heights Farms and manager of the We All Eat Market, said the idea came from conversations with residents about the absence of a grocery store."We were farming and we heard the call that the neighbor said, there hasn't been a grocery store in about 70 years, and we felt like we could do something about that because we can supply it with produce," Gooden said.How neighbourhood gardens led to a grocery storeFountain Heights Farms Cooperative started in 2016 with a plan to create a more sustainable food system in the community. Its work began with neighbourhood gardens and has since grown into a network of 16 farm plots. The cooperative aims to expand this network to 119 plots by 2030.The organisation works to connect local farmers, food producers and consumers. It also wants residents to take part in the local food business rather than remain only customers.The idea of opening a grocery store gained support from residents who wanted easier access to fresh food. Gooden said the cooperative approached neighbours and invited them to contribute towards the project.People responded with small cash contributions. According to Gooden, residents handed over $1, $5, $10 and $20 notes directly from their cars. These contributions helped the organisers raise $30,000 in 2021.The money was used to begin a capital campaign aimed at raising $1 million to construct the building. The city of Birmingham also contributed $150,000 towards the project.The community's early contributions helped demonstrate local support for the proposed store. After years of work, the cooperative was able to bring the project to completion.What the new market will offerThe We All Eat Market will sell Alabama-grown produce, meat, eggs and everyday grocery items. The cooperative wants to give residents access to locally sourced food while also providing small farmers and food businesses with more opportunities to reach customers.The market is also expected to become part of a wider distribution system for local food producers. The cooperative plans to transition its community-supported agriculture programme, commonly known as CSA, into a delivery service called We All Eat Delivery.This will give customers another way to purchase locally sourced food. It will also help small farmers and food entrepreneurs reach more buyers.Affordability is another important part of the market's plans. The store will accept Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program benefits, known as SNAP or EBT. It will also participate in Auburn University's Double Up Bucks programme, which gives eligible customers a 50% discount on certain produce.The cooperative wants to make fresh food accessible to households that might otherwise choose cheaper options at larger grocery stores. Larger retailers often have greater buying power and can negotiate prices that smaller independent businesses may struggle to match.At the same time, the market wants to pay local farmers and producers fairly while keeping its operations financially sustainable.Cooperative co-founder Dominique Villanueva said the organisation wants to offer affordable food that also supports the community's health.Villanueva said the aim is to strike a balance between providing food people can afford and offering "food that nourishes our community and builds our health."Residents to have a stake in the local food systemThe cooperative's plans go beyond running a neighbourhood grocery store. It also wants residents to participate in ownership and benefit economically from the local food system.The market currently has three employees, while the farming operation employs five workers. The cooperative hopes its activities will create more opportunities as the business expands.However, setting up the store also involved practical challenges. The organisers had to deal with permits, local ordinances and regulations that were largely designed for traditional grocery retailers rather than urban farms.One example is the restriction on urban farms cutting and selling meat at their own premises.Despite these challenges, the cooperative has opened the market and hopes it will help more money spent on groceries remain within the neighbourhood. It also wants the store to become a place where residents can meet and local producers can find customers.Gooden said the community's support had encouraged the team to continue its work."It's fuel to keep going. It's a lot of hard work in farming. And what we also learn is in that hard work, you're going to see people come and help. And more and more we see more and more help. And today is just a celebration of that," he said.A model residents want to expandThe opening has also raised hopes that similar markets could be established in other parts of Birmingham.A community member said the city needed more neighbourhood markets so residents would not have to travel far to buy groceries."I just think that we need to open these types of markets all over the 99 neighborhoods and if not the 99 neighborhoods, the 23 communities need to have one," the resident said.The We All Eat Market operates from Tuesday to Sunday and remains closed on Mondays for restocking.You use AI every day. articles.title: 'No power can threaten informed citizens': Ex-CDS Chauhan warns of cognitive warfare threat to India
articles.summary: Former chief of defence staff General Anil Chauhan has warned that India's national security challenges are increasingly extending beyond conventional
articles.body: Former chief of defence staff General Anil Chauhan has warned that India's national security challenges are increasingly extending beyond conventional military threats, with deepfakes, information manipulation and influence operations emerging as tools of cognitive warfare.He has called for making strategic thinking part of the country's education system, arguing that universities, citizens and society must play a greater role in strengthening national security.According to news agency ANI, Chauhan made the remarks while delivering the inaugural lecture on 'Strategic Culture of India and National Security' at Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU) on November 3. He stressed that strategic awareness should extend beyond the armed forces and government institutions to become part of India's broader national education framework."The first task is to make strategic thinking part of national education," Chauhan said.Cognitive warfare and the threat to national securityHighlighting the changing nature of warfare, Chauhan identified cognitive warfare as a growing threat, pointing to the use of deepfakes, manipulated information, influence operations and social media to shape public perception and influence societies.He cautioned that such operations could create divisions within society by influencing public opinion before facts are verified. He said the challenge should not be treated merely as a battle of narratives or a public relations exercise."Cognitive warfare is not just a battle of narrative nor it is public relations exercise. Its understanding must become part of national resilience building," he said.The former CDS also called for stronger links between universities and military war colleges, arguing that subjects such as Indian political thought, statecraft, military history, diplomacy, technology and national security should become part of academic discourse.Chauhan's remarks reflect the expanding definition of national security, which is no longer confined to territorial defence or military preparedness. The growing use of information, technology and economic dependencies as instruments of geopolitical pressure has made societal awareness an important part of a country's resilience.Emphasising the role of citizens, he said national security depended on an informed population capable of recognising emerging threats."No power, I repeat, no power can threaten the frontiers of a nation whose citizens are aware and informed," he said.He also highlighted the importance of combining India's traditional strategic thinking with contemporary security requirements. Referring to dharma and Kautilya's principles of statecraft, Chauhan said India must maintain ethical restraint while remaining strategically prepared.On the growing use of economic instruments in strategic competition, Chauhan warned that interdependence itself was increasingly being used as leverage."Economic interdependence is being weaponised. Trade, finance, critical minerals, energy, technology, standards, supply chains, data, information. Everything is weaponised today," he said.He further stressed that Indian strategic thought should be communicated in languages accessible to the wider population, saying national security awareness must reach beyond academic and military institutions.

articles.title: Michael Jackson’s iconic stage glove sells for €113,737 at French auction, while a black sequinned jacket fetches €75,825 as nearly 50 rare costumes, autographs and personal belongings go under the hammer
articles.summary: Michael Jackson's iconic stage gloves, sequinned jackets and personal belongings have found new owners after going under the hammer at a French auction,
articles.body: Michael Jackson's iconic stage gloves, sequinned jackets and personal belongings have found new owners after going under the hammer at a French auction, with one glove selling for an impressive €113,737. The June 3 sale, organised by French auction house Aguttes in Neuilly-sur-Seine, brought around 50 objects associated with the late King of Pop to the auction floor. Among the highlights were a black sequinned stage jacket that fetched €75,825 and a T-shirt linked to his Scream music video, which sold for €24,011. The collection also included rare costume pieces, autographs, drawings and personal belongings.What was Michael Jackson's €1 million memorabilia collection worthAccording to an official announcement by Aguttes, the collection originally belonged to Norwegian collector Richard Fossaas, who assembled the objects with the intention of developing a future museum project. The collection subsequently passed into the hands of a private collector in New York before being presented in Paris for the auction.Aguttes described the collection as a selection of approximately 50 objects that once belonged to Jackson. The pieces included stage costumes, accessories, autographs and drawings, offering a look at different periods of the singer's career. The auction house valued the collection at between €500,000 and €1 million, with individual estimates ranging from €400 to more than €100,000.Michael Jackson's iconic stage glove sells for €113,737One of the most notable items in the auction was a right-hand stage glove associated with Jackson's performances. Listed as Lot 14, the glove was estimated to sell for between €100,000 and €150,000. According to Aguttes' published auction results, it eventually sold for €113,737.The collection also included a black sequinned stage jacket, listed as Lot 10, which had an estimate of €50,000 to €70,000 and sold for €75,825. Another left-hand stage glove, listed as Lot 24, fetched €36,648 against an estimate of €30,000 to €40,000. A second left-hand glove, Lot 43, sold for €32,857, according to the auction house's results.Michael Jackson's rare Pepsi jacket and Dior cardigan go under the hammerAmong the other notable pieces was a black Dexter Wong T-shirt associated with Jackson's Scream music video. Listed as Lot 21, the garment carried an estimate of €20,000 to €30,000 and eventually sold for €24,011. The auction also featured clothing and accessories linked to the singer's stage appearances and collaborations with designers.Other objects included a rare black sequinned jacket prototype connected to a Pepsi campaign, a red Dior cardigan, worn shirts, autograph drawings and a personal pillow. Aguttes also highlighted pieces attributed to costume designer Bill Whitten and prototypes associated with Jackson's stage wardrobe. The selection brought together both performance-related memorabilia and objects connected to the singer's personal life.Jackson's career celebrated through rare memorabilia exhibitionBefore the auction, Aguttes organised a public exhibition from May 30 to June 2, 2026, at its Neuilly-sur-Seine premises. The exhibition was structured around three periods of Jackson's career. The first section, covering 1979 to 1984, focused on his early solo years and the success of Thriller, while the second covered 1987 to 1995, including his major international tours and commercial success.The final section covered 1996 to 2003 and included objects associated with the later years of his career and charitable activities. Aguttes also organised guided tours and talks on May 30, 2026, featuring Michael Jackson biographer Richard Lecoq. The public auction subsequently took place on June 3 at 6 pm at Aguttes in Neuilly-sur-Seine.Disclaimer: This article is based on information publicly available, including details released by Aguttes auction house. The Times of India has not independently verified the authenticity, provenance, ownership history or sale prices of the memorabilia mentioned. articles.title: An Ohio truck driver who lives near a proposed $5 billion Amazon data center has helped advance a township-wide ban on such facilities; a November 10 hearing could become the project's next major obstacle
articles.summary: A local truck driver who lives half a mile from a proposed $5 billion Amazon data center in Butler County, Ohio, has led a community campaign that could
articles.body: A local truck driver who lives half a mile from a proposed $5 billion Amazon data center in Butler County, Ohio, has led a community campaign that could stop the technology giant's major expansion. Barry Blankenship, a resident of St. Clair Township and a key organizer with the Woodsdale and Trenton Environmental Resistance group, has led efforts to block the large computing project. A major hearing scheduled for 10 November before the Butler County Rural Zoning Commission is the latest important challenge facing the development. The proposed project, planned by Amazon Web Services, would include an 18-building data center spread across 600 acres of farmland between Wayne Madison Road and Hawkins Road.Township zoning commission pushes for data center banOpposition to the multi-billion-dollar project reached an important stage when the St. Clair Township Zoning Commission passed a resolution calling for a complete ban on data centers within its zoning area. The recommendation was then sent to the Butler County Rural Zoning Commission, which scheduled a public review for 10 November at 3:00 p.m. While the county commission reviews the proposal, the final decision will belong to St. Clair Township's three trustees. They will hold a later public meeting to cast the final vote. The campaign against large computing facilities reflects growing concerns among local residents about water use, noise and pressure on public utilities. People opposing the project say the data center could threaten local groundwater supplies and the electrical grid. They also worry about pollution from backup generators used to keep the facility running."They couldn't give me any good answers, and I tell you what, I don't want them here," Blankenship said during a recent public information meeting, as reported by local public radio station WVXU. Other residents have also spoken out about the size and possible effects of the development."We're not opposed to growth. We're not opposed if it was a warehouse or something that doesn't suck your water dry, that won't burn your electric up... [that] won't make all the noise, and when they fire up the generators, all the pollution and everything," said local resident Joe Deaton, who lives near the proposed site, in comments published by WVXU. "We just don't want this."Amazon campaign meets voter resistanceAs public opposition continued to grow, Amazon Web Services held a "science fair" at Edgewood Middle School in October 2026. The event was designed to share environmental studies and project details directly with nearby residents. Company representatives said their goal was to provide clear information rather than influence public opinion. However, the company's information campaign did little to reduce growing opposition to data centers across the region. During the 3 November 2026 elections, voters in nearby Trenton approved a charter amendment banning data centers larger than 25 megawatts. The measure passed with 80 percent support, according to unofficial election results reported by WVXU. The opposition in Butler County is part of a wider change across Ohio. At least 14 municipalities and townships across the state approved local restrictions or bans on large data centers during the November 2026 elections, according to media outlet Fortune.Higher electricity bills and the large amounts of power needed to run artificial intelligence infrastructure became major concerns for voters supporting these restrictions. The Ohio Manufacturers' Association disagreed with claims that data centers directly lead to higher electricity prices for household customers. Amazon, meanwhile, said its long-term investment plans in the communities where it operates had not changed.Legal and annexation hurdles build upThe fight over the 600-acre property has also become more complicated because of changes to municipal boundaries and disagreements over attempts to annex the land. The City of Trenton had earlier considered bringing the proposed site into its city limits by annexing the land from St. Clair Township. This would have helped make room for the Amazon Web Services data center. However, local opposition grew stronger. Residents, including Blankenship and leaders of activist groups, organized petitions and other public campaigns against the move. Following this pressure, Trenton withdrew its annexation request before the scheduled public hearings, according to the City of Trenton's municipal council meeting minutes.With the annexation plan on hold and Trenton voters strongly supporting limits on large data centers, the proposed development remains subject to St. Clair Township's zoning rules. The county zoning hearing scheduled for 10 November will consider whether the township's proposed ban meets local land-use requirements. If the county commission approves the restriction, the three St. Clair Township trustees will hold the final vote on whether to make it official. If approved, the ban could effectively stop Amazon's $5 billion data center project at its proposed location.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.
